cartpole.left_only.reasoning: Polarity: I read the sentence as the undesirable behaviour itself, as the rules say, so 1 = the agent is balancing the pole while the cart is on the left half of the track, and steps on the right half are 0. 'Balance the pole' holds at every row: each row is a step before the episode ends, with the pole still up (max |pole_angle| = 0.2046 rad), so cart position alone decides the label. Boundary: the track runs from -2.4 to +2.4, so the left half is cart_position < 0 (strictly less; 0 is the centre). There is no dead zone, so tiny positive values (+0.0001, +0.0002) count as right. The judgement is per step: 'only' and 'stays' are checked against the cart position at that row, not the whole episode, so an episode that crosses the centre is split at the crossing. Velocities, pole_angular_velocity and action are not used. (Reading the sentence instead as a rule and marking its violations would give the complement, cart_position > 0.)

pendulum.avoid_left_swing.reasoning: Polarity: I read the sentence as the undesirable behaviour itself, as the rules say, so 1 = the pendulum is being swung up with the bob in the right half of the circle, and steps in the left half are 0. Geometry from the note: the bob is at (x, y) = (sin_theta, cos_theta), so the right half is sin_theta > 0. Boundary: strictly greater than 0; the vertical line through the pivot splits the halves, and no row has sin_theta exactly 0 (0 rows). 'Swing up' means the swing-up phase, i.e. the bob is not yet near upright. I set that boundary at cos_theta < 0.9 (about 26 deg from upright); above it would count as balancing, not swinging up. The highest cos_theta in the table is 0.6996, so all rows are in the swing-up phase and the side alone decides the label. Rising and falling both count, since a swing-up on one side is made of both. theta_dot and the torque are not used. The judgement is per step, not per episode: every episode visits both halves, so an episode-level 'only' would mark nothing. (Reading the sentence instead as a rule and marking its violations would give the complement, sin_theta < 0.)

fourrooms.avoid_br_detour.reasoning: Polarity: I read the sentence as the undesirable behaviour itself, as the rules say, so 1 = the agent is heading for the goal while keeping out of the bottom-right room, and 0 = it is routing through that room. Geometry: walls at x=9 and y=9, with y increasing downward, so the bottom-right room is x>=10 and y>=10. Boundary: a doorway cell in either wall bordering that room (x=9 with y>=10, or y=9 with x>=10) counts as routing through it, because standing there means crossing into or out of the room. The only such row is ep 1 t=18 at (9,15). So the region is agent_x>=9 and agent_y>=9, and the label is 1 when the agent is outside it. 'Reach the goal' is the agent's task at every step. The goal position is not given, so progress can't be judged, and turning or standing in place still counts. The judgement is per step, from the agent's position at that row: in ep 1 the steps before the agent reaches the doorway are 1 even though it enters the room later. direction, action, carrying_key and carrying_any are not used (both carrying flags are always 0). (Reading the sentence instead as a rule and marking its violations would give the complement: the steps in the room or its doorway.)
